subject.title: Gateway watchdog fails to kill stuck model calls; stall recovery is none

question: Should this issue continue to require a single core fix for active model-call abort plus restart replay dedupe, or should maintainers split the remaining replay/dedupe behavior after landing narrower diagnostic cleanup?
rationale: Current code and open PRs show partial fixes, but changing abort defaults and replay semantics can affect slow providers and existing session recovery behavior, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Keep canonical and split remainders
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, review the narrow diagnostic PRs, and split restart replay/dedupe into a focused follow-up only if maintainers want separate ownership.

options.title: Lower abort defaults in core
options.body: Treat the reported 120s expectation as the desired default and require upgrade proof for slow silent providers before merge.

options.title: Preserve shipped safety floor
options.body: Keep the 5-minute active-abort floor and document/operator-route the faster recovery request instead of changing core defaults now.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and split remainders
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, review the narrow diagnostic PRs, and split restart replay/dedupe into a focused follow-up only if maintainers want separate ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame routes the active model-call recovery gate through this history boundary, and the issue needs a maintainer-level decision on core diagnostic defaults.
